A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same retrieval framework, renamed from LLM2GR to MindRef. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval and downstream-task experiments on six KILT datasets, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, model comparisons, and retrieval cases.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–6, Figures 4–9, and the appendix case studies.

M1.justification: MindRef retains LLM2GR's Trie-constrained title recall, FM-index-constrained passage recall, weighted scoring, and short-prefix localization using KMP. The rewritten description does not establish a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, ELI5, FEVER, and Wizard of Wikipedia, covering the same question-answering, fact-checking, and dialogue tasks. No additional evaluated domain or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain BM25, Contriever, DPR, the retrieval-free Llama-2-13b reader, and the same Llama/Vicuna variants. Newly cited methods in Related Work are not added to the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: The validation splits, dataset sizes, metrics, model sizes, prompts, and stated decoding settings are retained, including beam sizes 15/10, k=2, a 16-token prefix, a 150-token reference, and alpha=0.9. Revised plotted values do not establish a protocol change or rerun.

E4.justification: The same ablations, sensitivity questions, fine-tuning comparisons, memory analysis, and six cases remain. However, the sensitivity evidence in Figures 4–9 is revised; notably, Figure 5 replaces the TriviaQA passage-retrieval dip at an 8-token prefix with an increase.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly states that all experimental results come from a single run. v3 retains the hardware statement but omits the run count. Neither version provides confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and 6 retain all numerical entries, but Figures 4–9 contain changes beyond rounding. For example, Figure 5's TriviaQA Answer in Context at an 8-token prefix changes from approximately 66.5 to 68.2, and at 16 tokens from 68.2 to 68.8. These are revised plotted results under unchanged stated settings.

T1.justification: v3 removes Section 2.2's explicit O(V log V) bound for obtaining permissible successor tokens from the FM-index. Equations 1–3 and the appendix Trie/BWT/FM-index explanations remain mathematically equivalent; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central retrieval contribution remains, but v3 strengthens the introduction with claims of first formalizing document-to-detail memory in neural architectures, state-of-the-art performance, and '95%+ accuracy.' Its 4x speedup and FEVER 78.79% statements highlight existing results; the 95% claim lacks a specified supporting evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 retains the principal limitations concerning document titles, pretraining coverage, and knowledge updates. However, it removes v2 Appendix F's specific explanation that RLHF-induced polite openings such as 'Sure!' interfere with constrained recall, replacing the detailed fine-tuning discussion with the broader existing summary.

D1.justification: v3 adds a MindRef code-repository link, whereas v2 only supplies baseline implementation links. Conversely, v3 leaves 'the library' unidentified where v2 cited Transformers. Core hyperparameters, hardware, prompts, preprocessing, and dataset-license information remain available.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Tang et al. (2024) and Yue et al. (2025), while removing several cited works and their discussion, including Ziems et al. (2023), Liu et al. (2022), and Sun et al. (2023). The broad sparse, dense, and generative retrieval positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, method explanation, related work, and conclusion are substantially condensed and rewritten. The framework, title, and author information change, while v2's separate experimental appendices and main-text Further Analysis are consolidated into Appendix B and its subsections.

P2.justification: Tables 1–4 shrink from full-width to single-column displays, and Tables 1–3 replace bold/underlined rankings with cyan/pink highlighting. Figure 1 is rearranged, Figures 2–3 are substantially reduced, and Figures 4–9 are restyled and packed more tightly, changing axes, legends, and readability.

improvement.justification: The code link and condensed organization are useful, but v3 omits the single-run disclosure and introduces an unexplained '95%+ accuracy' claim. Revised plots also weaken internal consistency: Figure 5's default 16-token TriviaQA result is about 68.8, while Table 2 remains 68.20; these agreed in v2. Smaller main tables further reduce readability. These limited losses in transparency and evidence alignment outweigh the presentation and access benefits.
